newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Naphtha/Mogas - Mogas firms despite Taiwan.
newsitem.headline: Asia Naphtha/Mogas - Mogas firms despite Taiwan.

text.p: Gasoline prices on Wednesday edged up on trader buying in the Singapore market despite the low Taiwan reformate awards.

Taiwan's state-owned Chinese Petroleum Corp (CPC) bought two unleaded 95-octane reformate cargoes for May 16-31 and June 1-15 delivery at $24.60 and $24.70 per barrel respectively, c-and-f, a company official said.
Traders said the May cargo was awarded to Dutch trader Vitol and the June cargo to South Korean refiner Yukong.
But a second May 16-31 unleaded cargo might be awarded to a Japanese trader, they said.

The tender, which closed April 21 and was valid for two days, sought a 250,000-barrel cargo of unleaded reformate for delivery May 16-31 and/or June 1-15 and a 250,000-barrel cargo of leaded reformate for June 1-15 arrival.
CPC already awarded the leaded cargo on Tuesday at $25.20 per barrel on a cost-and-freight (c-and-f) basis to Keelung, Taichung, Kaohsiung or Shalung to Vitol, sources said.
They said CPC had delayed the unleaded award to Wednesday as it asked sellers of the May cargo who had submitted offers ranging between $25.00 to $25.50 to match the low offer for the June cargo.
"It is very low...but Singapore prices are not depressed by it because there is a trader bidding up the market," a trader said on the awards.
A Dutch trader bought 50,000-barrels of 97-octane lifting mid-May at $24.50 per barrel, fob, 50 cents higher than Tuesday's deal.
The same trader bid the 92-octane grade at $23.85.
The naphtha market was hit by some jitters on talk of problems at India's Reliance ethylene plant.
But a spokesman told Reuters "All the Reliance plants are working at normal capacity and there is no single untoward incidents at any of the sights".
He said there was a local fire in the area which sparked off the rummours but which had nothing to do with any of Reliance's facilities.
Naphtha swaps were weaker with overnight crude with May and June last quoted at $21.20/$21.30 per barrel.
(Prices are in dollars per barrel)
